accuracy.evidence: Spectra rounded from NIST Chemistry WebBook electron-ionisation data: pentane base 43 with M⁺ 72 ~10%; ethanol base 31, 45 ~51%, M⁺ 46 ~22%; propanone base 43, M⁺ 58 ~64%; hexane base 57, M⁺ 86 ~15%; butane base 43, M⁺ 58 ~12%; benzene M⁺ 78 = base, 79 at 6.6%; propane base 29, M⁺ 44; propan-1-ol base 31, M⁺ 60 weak; butan-1-ol M⁺ 74 ~2%. M+1 heights follow 1.1% per carbon (hexane 6.6% of 15 ≈ 1.0). Every Mr recomputed with C 12, H 1, O 16 (C3H7OH 60, C4H9OH 74, C3H6O 58, C4H10 58, C2H5OH 46). Fragment losses 72 − 57 = 15 (CH3), 72 − 43 = 29 (C2H5), 46 − 31 = 15. Specification wording checked against AQA 7405 and OCR A H432.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in AQA and OCR examiner reports: taking the tallest (base) peak as M⁺, taking the tiny M+1 peak as M⁺ because it has the highest m/z, forgetting the H in OH when adding formula masses (C2H5OH vs C2H6), thinking a fragment can be heavier than M⁺, mixing up the lost piece with the fragment (57 vs 43 for CH3 vs C2H5), and assuming the same M⁺ means the same compound (butane and propanone, both 58).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmion works only on reading the molecular ion in a finished spectrum: pick M⁺ past base-peak and M+1 decoys in nine NIST-shaped spectra, add up formula masses to name unknowns, find fragment peaks by mass lost, and judge pairs of spectra including a same-Mr pair. flagtof simulates the spectrometer hardware (ionise, accelerate, flight tube); flaginstr chooses between instruments and only touches M⁺ once. Shingle gate passed under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner is shown spectra where the tallest peak is a fragment and must find that the whole-molecule peak sits furthest right; the M+1 step then adds hexane and butane where a 1% peak sits beyond M⁺, and benzene where M⁺ is the base peak, so 'highest m/z apart from M+1' is earned rather than told; naming unknowns forces the Mr arithmetic; the fragment step shows every fragment lies left of M⁺; the last pair shows M⁺ cannot separate butane and propanone.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 'the tallest peak' gives Mr (disproved by pentane's base peak at 43), '87 because it has the highest m/z' for hexane (it is the carbon-13 peak), 'a big fragment can be above M⁺' (no peak ever appears right of M⁺ except M+1), and 'different formulas give different M⁺' for butane and propanone (both 58).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers: '43 is the base peak, the most common fragment'; 'the tiny peak one above M⁺ is the M+1 peak from carbon-13'; 'C2H6 is 30, not 46' and 'C3H8 is 44'; '72 − 57 = 15, which is CH3; losing C2H5 would give 43'; 'losing an electron makes M⁺ itself'; 'same Mr does not mean same compound'. In-lab misses explain the picked peak (base peak, fragment, M+1, M⁺ itself) with the subtraction worked out.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py readability passed: kid text FK 3.2 (limit 6.5), adult text FK 8.9 (limit 9.5). Kid paragraphs carry one worked case each (pentane at 72, the 1-in-90 carbon-13 ratio, butane and propanone at 58). Precise terms are used and defined: molecular ion M⁺, m/z, Mr, base peak, fragment ion, M+1 peak, carbon-13, and the ionisation equation in the adult text.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with the mass spectrometer and instrumental analysis lessons is under the 12% limit. Every sentence states a rule about M⁺, a number to check it with, or a named mistake; the adult text adds specification links, the ionisation equation, notes on weak alcohol M⁺ and benzene's base peak, and what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark for every step before and after Show me. Bars are at least 4 px wide and tiny peaks are drawn at 3 px so the M+1 and weak alcohol M⁺ stay visible; the selected peak shows its m/z above it; the m/z axis labels every 20 above m/z 70 so labels never collide; formula cards and the A / B / cannot-tell boxes are full-width tap targets; the two small spectra in the last step fit side by side.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every Show me finished, the challenge rendered, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark, and there were no console or page errors. Peaks can be reached with ◀ Peak / Peak ▶ and chosen with 'Choose this peak'; formulas and spectrum choices have their own buttons; the canvas aria-label reads each peak, e.g. 'm/z 43, 100% of the tallest peak. This is the base peak.'
